decisions.rationale: Leading Charizard and Venusaur allows Mega Charizard Y to set Drought and immediately activate Venusaur's Chlorophyll, granting speed control and immense offensive pressure against Whimsicott, Politoed, and Basculegion. Dragapult provides fast physical spectral cleanup against Delphox and Basculegion, while Hisuian Goodra serves as a super-bulky defensive pivot against special threats.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Brought Charizard Y, Venusaur, Dragapult, Goodra-Hisui vs Whimsicott/Basculegion/Delphox/Politoed/Tsareena/Metagross. Plan is Drought + Chlorophyll lead pressure, into Dragapult/Goodra-Hisui cleanup.

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott + Metagross for Tailwind pressure and a guaranteed Rock Slide OHKO on Mega Charizard Y. Keep Politoed in back to overwrite sun after Mega evolution and enable Basculegion’s Swift Swim endgame. This four also avoids exposing Politoed to an unfavorable opening weather sequence.
decisions.notebook: Core matchup plan: Whimsicott + Metagross is the preferred lead into Charizard sun; Tailwind supports Metagross, whose spread Rock Slide guarantees an OHKO on Mega Charizard Y. Hold Politoed in back so Drizzle can overwrite Drought after Charizard Mega Evolves, then preserve Basculegion for a rain-enabled late-game sweep. Watch for Tinkaton Fake Out/Feint disrupting Whimsicott or Protect lines, Venusaur doubling Speed under sun, and Garganacl using Wide Guard against Rock Slide. Tsareena remains an alternative in later games if priority denial or stronger pressure into Garganacl/Goodra-Hisui becomes more important.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolving Charizard sets Sun, boosting Venusaur's Speed to 256 via Chlorophyll. Venusaur outspeeds Metagross even under Prankster Tailwind and hits Metagross with Weather Ball (93-171% damage), guaranteed KOing alongside Charizard's Heat Wave. Heat Wave also strips Whimsicott's Focus Sash.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Brought Charizard Y, Venusaur, Dragapult, Goodra-Hisui vs Whimsicott/Basculegion/Delphox/Politoed/Tsareena/Metagross. Plan: Drought + Chlorophyll lead pressure, into Dragapult/Goodra-Hisui cleanup.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind plus Protect avoids Metagross being OHKOed by sun-boosted Heat Wave or Venusaur Weather Ball. Next turn, Politoed can enter after Drought is already established, overwrite sun with rain, remove Chlorophyll, and let Tailwind Metagross pressure Charizard safely.
decisions.notebook: Core matchup plan: Lead Whimsicott + Metagross into Charizard/Venusaur. Prefer Tailwind + Metagross Protect initially because both sun-boosted Heat Wave and Venusaur Weather Ball can OHKO Metagross. Once Mega Charizard Y has activated Drought, bring Politoed in to overwrite it with rain; then Tailwind Metagross can outspeed both foes and threaten Charizard with 4x-effective Rock Slide. Preserve Basculegion for a rain-enabled late-game sweep. Watch for Garganacl Wide Guard blocking Rock Slide and Tinkaton Fake Out/Feint disrupting support or Protect lines. Tsareena remains a later-game alternative if priority denial or better pressure into Garganacl/Goodra-Hisui is needed.

decisions.rationale: Charizard uses Protect to stay safe against Metagross's potential 4x Rock Slide and negate any switch-in risks (such as Politoed overriding sun). Under sun, Venusaur's Chlorophyll gives it 256 effective Speed, comfortably outspeeding Metagross in Tailwind (180-244). Venusaur's sun-boosted Life Orb Weather Ball deals 93-171% to Metagross, giving a high chance for a clean OHKO before Metagross can act.
decisions.notebook:
Game 1: Brought Charizard-Y, Venusaur, Dragapult, Goodra-Hisui vs Whimsicott/Basculegion/Delphox/Politoed/Tsareena/Metagross.
Opponent sets:
- Whimsicott: Focus Sash (consumed G1T1), Prankster, Tailwind, Taunt, Encore, Moonblast, Timid.
- Metagross: Shuca Berry, Clear Body, Meteor Mash, Stomping Tantrum, Rock Slide, Protect, Adamant.
- Politoed: Sitrus Berry, Drizzle, Calm.
- Basculegion: Life Orb, Swift Swim, Adamant.
- Delphox: Delphoxite (Mega), Levitate, Timid.
- Tsareena: Wide Lens, Queenly Majesty, Adamant.

Strategy: Use Sun + Chlorophyll Speed advantage to pressure foes. Protect Charizard against Rock Slide/weather shifts when Tailwind is up.

decisions.rationale: Switching Politoed immediately replaces sun with rain, removes Chlorophyll’s Speed boost, and lets Tailwind Metagross move before both foes. Rock Slide then guarantees the Charizard KO if it connects while also damaging Venusaur; rain also sharply reduces their Fire pressure.
decisions.notebook: Core plan: lead Whimsicott + Metagross into Charizard/Venusaur, establish Tailwind, then pivot Politoed in after Mega Charizard Y sets sun. Rain removes Chlorophyll acceleration, weakens Fire attacks, and enables Tailwind Metagross to pressure Charizard with 4x-effective Rock Slide. Preserve Basculegion for a rain-enabled late-game sweep. Rock Slide is a guaranteed OHKO on Mega Charizard Y if it connects, though its 90% accuracy and possible Protect must be respected. Watch for Garganacl Wide Guard blocking Rock Slide and Tinkaton Fake Out/Feint disrupting support or Protect lines. Tsareena is a later-game alternative when priority denial or stronger pressure into Garganacl/Goodra-Hisui is needed.

decisions.rationale: Both foes outspeed in Tailwind and threaten massive damage on Charizard (Weather Ball/Rock Slide) and Venusaur (Icy Wind/Rock Slide). Charizard's Protect has reduced accuracy after turn 2. Switching Charizard to Goodra-Hisui double-resists Water and resists Rock, while Venusaur uses Protect to stay healthy and stall Tailwind turns.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Brought Charizard-Y, Venusaur, Dragapult, Goodra-Hisui vs Whimsicott/Basculegion/Delphox/Politoed/Tsareena/Metagross. Opponent sets: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster, Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast, Timid), Metagross (Shuca Berry, Clear Body, Meteor Mash/Stomping Tantrum/Rock Slide/Protect, Adamant), Politoed (Sitrus Berry, Drizzle, Calm), Basculegion (Life Orb, Swift Swim, Adamant), Delphox (Delphoxite, Levitate, Timid), Tsareena (Wide Lens, Queenly Majesty, Adamant). Strategy: Protect/switch to stall Tailwind/Rain, then reset Sun with Charizard to reclaim Speed advantage.

decisions.rationale: Double-pressure Charizard before either foe can move. Rock Slide guarantees the OHKO if it connects, while rain-boosted Weather Ball provides strong backup against a miss. Rock Slide also chips or may flinch Venusaur if Charizard Protects.
decisions.notebook: Core plan: use Whimsicott Tailwind, then pivot Politoed into Mega Charizard Y's sun to establish rain, remove Venusaur's Chlorophyll boost, weaken Fire attacks, and enable Basculegion. Tailwind Metagross outspeeds Charizard/Venusaur and Rock Slide guarantees an OHKO on Mega Charizard Y if it connects. Preserve Basculegion for a rain-enabled late-game sweep. Respect Rock Slide's 90% accuracy, Charizard Protect, Garganacl Wide Guard, and Tinkaton Fake Out/Feint. Against Charizard/Venusaur, prioritize removing Charizard while rain suppresses their Fire/sun pressure; use Icy Wind when Tailwind is ending if continued speed control is needed.

decisions.rationale: Switching Charizard-Y sets Sun via Drought, immediately activating Chlorophyll on Venusaur to boost its Speed to 256 (outspeeding both opposing foes under Tailwind). In Sun, Venusaur's Weather Ball becomes a Fire-type move boosted by Sun and Life Orb that hits Metagross for 93-171% (bypassing Shuca Berry) before it can move. Charizard entering also grants Ground immunity against potential Stomping Tantrum. Opposing Tailwind expires at the end of this turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Brought Charizard-Y, Venusaur, Dragapult, Goodra-Hisui vs Whimsicott/Basculegion/Delphox/Politoed/Tsareena/Metagross. Opponent sets: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster, Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast, Timid), Metagross (Shuca Berry, Clear Body, Meteor Mash/Stomping Tantrum/Rock Slide/Protect, Adamant), Politoed (Sitrus Berry, Drizzle, Calm), Basculegion (Life Orb, Swift Swim, Adamant), Delphox (Delphoxite, Levitate, Timid), Tsareena (Wide Lens, Queenly Majesty, Adamant). Strategy: Stall Tailwind/Rain, then reset Sun with Charizard to reclaim Speed advantage with Chlorophyll Venusaur.

decisions.rationale: Icy Wind preserves speed control after Tailwind expires and chips both foes. Meteor Mash targets Venusaur for a guaranteed KO from its shown range if it hits, preventing major Grass pressure. Rain also limits Goodra’s Flamethrower retaliation.
decisions.notebook: Core plan: establish Tailwind with Whimsicott, pivot Politoed into Charizard’s sun to restore rain, suppress Fire damage and Chlorophyll, then preserve Basculegion for a rain-enabled endgame. Tailwind Metagross outspeeds Charizard/Venusaur; Rock Slide can OHKO Mega Charizard Y if it connects. Respect Rock Slide/Meteor Mash accuracy, Charizard Protect, Garganacl Wide Guard, and Tinkaton Fake Out/Feint. When Tailwind is expiring, use Icy Wind to maintain speed control. Metagross Stomping Tantrum is the strongest listed option into Hisuian Goodra but may miss the KO from moderate health; rain weakens Goodra’s Flamethrower.

decisions.rationale: Bring Whimsicott to restore priority Tailwind support while preserving Basculegion for the rain endgame. Sending Basculegion directly into sun leaves it slower than Chlorophyll Venusaur and exposed to Solar Beam.
decisions.notebook: Core plan: use Whimsicott’s priority Tailwind and Politoed’s rain control to remove Chlorophyll, weaken Fire attacks, and enable Swift Swim Basculegion. Preserve Basculegion as the primary cleaner; avoid exposing it to sun-boosted Venusaur before rain or speed control is established. Opponent has revealed Charizard-Mega-Y, Venusaur, and Goodra-Hisui; fourth remains unknown. Charizard’s sun can overwrite Drizzle whenever it enters, so Rain Dance may be needed without pivoting. Icy Wind provides backup speed control. Respect Charizard Protect, Venusaur Protect, Goodra’s bulk, Garganacl Wide Guard, and Tinkaton Fake Out/Feint.

decisions.rationale: Charizard uses Heat Wave to KO 1 HP Whimsicott and chip Politoed. Venusaur uses Solar Beam on Politoed, dealing 90.4-160.6% damage in Sun before Politoed can use Rain Dance. Combined damage guarantees a KO on Politoed if it doesn't Protect, while eliminating Whimsicott regardless.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Brought Charizard-Y, Venusaur, Dragapult, Goodra-Hisui vs Whimsicott/Basculegion/Delphox/Politoed/Tsareena/Metagross. Opponent sets: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster, Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast, Timid), Metagross (Shuca Berry, Clear Body, Meteor Mash/Stomping Tantrum/Rock Slide/Protect, Adamant), Politoed (Sitrus Berry, Drizzle, Calm), Basculegion (Life Orb, Swift Swim, Adamant), Delphox (Delphoxite, Levitate, Timid), Tsareena (Wide Lens, Queenly Majesty, Adamant). Strategy: Maintain Sun to leverage Chlorophyll Venusaur and boosted Fire attacks; eliminate rain setter Politoed to lock out Swift Swim Basculegion.

selection: Rain Dance (all adjacent, including ally Whimsicott)
decisions.rationale: Encore locks Venusaur into Weather Ball before it acts, preventing Solar Beam into Politoed. Rain Dance then removes Chlorophyll and sun while making the locked Weather Ball Water-type; Politoed survives even Charizard Solar Beam plus sun Weather Ball ranges. This safely enables Swift Swim Basculegion.
decisions.notebook: Core plan: combine Politoed rain control with Swift Swim Basculegion; preserve Basculegion as the primary cleaner. Charizard-Mega-Y can overwrite Drizzle on entry, so use Rain Dance when necessary. Whimsicott supplies priority Tailwind, Taunt, and Encore. Opponent revealed Charizard-Mega-Y, Venusaur, and Goodra-Hisui in game 1; fourth remains unknown. Venusaur carries Life Orb and Chlorophyll with Sludge Bomb, Solar Beam, Weather Ball, Protect. Charizard has Heat Wave, Solar Beam, Scorching Sands, Protect. Goodra-Hisui has Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Flamethrower, Protect with Sitrus Berry and Sap Sipper. Respect Garganacl Wide Guard and Tinkaton Fake Out/Feint if brought.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Basculegion outspeeds both active slots in Rain via Swift Swim and threatens a lethal Wave Crash into Charizard-Mega-Y. Using Protect on Charizard safely blocks high-damage Water/Ghost STABs aimed at slot 1. Meanwhile, Venusaur is locked into Weather Ball by Encore; switching Venusaur to Goodra-Hisui takes advantage of Goodra's resistance to Water/Ice attacks, preserving Venusaur for when Sun can be re-established later.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Brought Charizard-Y, Venusaur, Dragapult, Goodra-Hisui vs Whimsicott/Basculegion/Delphox/Politoed/Tsareena/Metagross. Opponent sets: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster, Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast, Timid), Metagross (Shuca Berry, Clear Body, Meteor Mash/Stomping Tantrum/Rock Slide/Protect, Adamant), Politoed (Sitrus Berry, Drizzle, Weather Ball/Icy Wind/Rain Dance/Protect, Calm), Basculegion (Life Orb, Swift Swim, Wave Crash/Last Respects/Aqua Jet/Protect, Adamant), Delphox (Delphoxite, Levitate, Timid), Tsareena (Wide Lens, Queenly Majesty, Adamant). Plan: Preserve Charizard-Y to overwrite Rain with Sun via Drought so Chlorophyll Venusaur and Fire/Grass offense regain speed and pressure.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult enters at 100% HP with 213 Speed, offering immediate ghost/dragon offensive pressure, semi-invulnerability with Phantom Force, or burn support with Will-O-Wisp. Venusaur is at 32% HP and ineffective while Rain is active since Solar Beam requires a charge turn and Weather Ball becomes Water-type.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Brought Charizard-Y, Venusaur, Dragapult, Goodra-Hisui vs Whimsicott/Basculegion/Delphox/Politoed/Tsareena/Metagross. Opponent sets: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster, Timid), Metagross (Shuca Berry, Clear Body, Adamant), Politoed (Sitrus Berry, Drizzle, Calm), Basculegion (Life Orb, Swift Swim, Adamant). Plan: Preserve Charizard-Y to reset weather to Sun via Drought when needed, enabling Chlorophyll Venusaur and boosted Fire offense.

decisions.rationale: Last Respects guarantees the Venusaur KO while rain-boosted Weather Ball threatens Charizard with a possible KO from its shown range. This splits damage efficiently; even if Charizard survives or Protects, Basculegion remains positioned to finish it with priority next turn.
decisions.notebook: Core plan: pair Politoed rain control with Swift Swim Basculegion as the primary cleaner; preserve Basculegion when possible. Charizard-Mega-Y overwrites rain on Mega entry, so use Rain Dance after it is already Mega Evolved or when weather must be restored. Whimsicott provides priority Tailwind, Taunt, and Encore. Game 1 revealed Charizard-Mega-Y (Heat Wave, Solar Beam, Scorching Sands, Protect), Venusaur (Sludge Bomb, Solar Beam, Weather Ball, Protect; Life Orb/Chlorophyll), and Goodra-Hisui (Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Flamethrower, Protect; Sitrus Berry/Sap Sipper); fourth remains unknown. Respect Garganacl Wide Guard and Tinkaton Fake Out/Feint if brought. In rain, Politoed Weather Ball has a possible but non-guaranteed KO on Charizard from 91%, while Basculegion Wave Crash guarantees it. With two allies fainted, Last Respects guarantees Venusaur from 31%.

decisions.rationale: Charizard-Y is at -1 Speed in Rain and risks fainting to Aqua Jet/Wave Crash. Protect has a reduced success rate. Switching Charizard out to Venusaur preserves Charizard to reset weather to Sun later with Drought. Dragapult using Phantom Force on Basculegion allows Dragapult to vanish on turn 1 to dodge single-target attacks and strike Basculegion for super-effective damage next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Brought Charizard-Y, Venusaur, Dragapult, Goodra-Hisui vs Whimsicott/Basculegion/Delphox/Politoed/Tsareena/Metagross. Opponent sets: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster, Timid), Metagross (Shuca Berry, Clear Body, Adamant), Politoed (Sitrus Berry, Drizzle, Calm), Basculegion (Life Orb, Swift Swim, Adamant). Strategy: Preserve Charizard-Y to reset weather to Sun via Drought when needed, enabling Chlorophyll Venusaur and boosted Fire attacks against Politoed/Basculegion.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Basculegion outspeeds Dragapult and two fallen allies power Last Respects enough to secure the key knockout. Politoed simultaneously pressures Charizard with rain-boosted, super-effective Weather Ball; even if Charizard protects, Dragapult is removed and Charizard's consecutive Protect odds are reduced.
decisions.notebook: Core plan: use Politoed rain control with Swift Swim Basculegion as the primary cleaner; preserve Basculegion when practical. Charizard-Mega-Y overwrites rain on Mega entry, so restore rain after Mega Evolution. Whimsicott offers priority Tailwind, Taunt, and Encore. Game 1 revealed Charizard-Mega-Y (Heat Wave, Solar Beam, Scorching Sands, Protect), Venusaur (Sludge Bomb, Solar Beam, Weather Ball, Protect; Life Orb/Chlorophyll), Goodra-Hisui (Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Flamethrower, Protect; Sitrus Berry/Sap Sipper), and Dragapult (Phantom Force, Dragon Darts, U-turn, Will-O-Wisp; Spell Tag/Infiltrator). Respect Garganacl Wide Guard and Tinkaton Fake Out/Feint in later games. In rain, Politoed Weather Ball can threaten Charizard but is not always a guaranteed KO across hidden bulk; Basculegion Wave Crash guarantees it from 91%. With two allies fainted, boosted Last Respects is the preferred Dragapult removal and guarantees Venusaur from 31%.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur uses Protect to block potential Aqua Jet or targeted attacks and avoid dying to Life Orb recoil. Charizard-Mega-Y outspeeds Basculegion in Sun (148 vs 98-130) and uses Solar Beam into Basculegion (80% HP), which has a high probability of KOing Basculegion before it can deliver a boosted Last Respects. Politoed poses no immediate OHKO threat to Charizard in Sun.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Timid), Metagross (Shuca Berry, Adamant), Politoed (Sitrus Berry, Calm), Basculegion (Life Orb, Adamant). Delphox-Mega and Tsareena were left on bench. Politoed has Drizzle, Weather Ball, Icy Wind, Rain Dance, Protect. Basculegion has Life Orb, Swift Swim, Wave Crash, Last Respects, Aqua Jet, Protect.

selection: Rain Dance (all adjacent, including ally Basculegion)
decisions.rationale: Aqua Jet’s priority guarantees the Venusaur KO before it can attack. Rain Dance is then the strongest route to neutralize sun and enable Swift Swim, leaving Charizard as the sole foe and making Basculegion the likely cleaner if Politoed completes the weather change.
decisions.notebook: Core plan: use Politoed rain control with Swift Swim Basculegion as the primary cleaner; preserve Basculegion when practical. Charizard-Mega-Y overwrites rain on Mega entry, so restore rain after Mega Evolution. Whimsicott provides priority Tailwind, Taunt, and Encore. Game 1 revealed Charizard-Mega-Y with Heat Wave, Solar Beam, Scorching Sands, Protect; Venusaur with Sludge Bomb, Solar Beam, Weather Ball, Protect and Life Orb/Chlorophyll; Goodra-Hisui with Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Flamethrower, Protect and Sitrus Berry/Sap Sipper; Dragapult with Phantom Force, Dragon Darts, U-turn, Will-O-Wisp and Spell Tag/Infiltrator. Respect Garganacl Wide Guard and Tinkaton Fake Out/Feint in later games. In rain, Politoed Weather Ball threatens Charizard but is not always a guaranteed KO across hidden bulk; Basculegion Wave Crash guarantees it from 91%. With two allies fainted, boosted Last Respects is the preferred Dragapult removal.

decisions.rationale: Both Charizard-Mega-Y (148) and Venusaur (128) outspeed Politoed (90-122). In rain, Solar Beam requires a charge turn and Heat Wave is heavily nerfed. Scorching Sands (18.8-33.9%) plus Sludge Bomb (34.0-61.2%) combine for 52.8-95.1% total damage before Politoed can act, giving the highest probability of knocking out Politoed (77% HP) this turn to claim Game 1.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Timid), Metagross (Shuca Berry, Adamant), Politoed (Sitrus Berry, Calm), Basculegion (Life Orb, Adamant). Delphox-Mega and Tsareena left on bench. Politoed has Drizzle, Weather Ball, Icy Wind, Rain Dance, Protect. Basculegion has Life Orb, Swift Swim, Wave Crash, Last Respects, Aqua Jet, Protect.

decisions.rationale: Rain-boosted Weather Ball guarantees the Charizard KO if Politoed moves. Venusaur is nearly down and Life Orb recoil will remove it if it attacks; if it Protects, Charizard still falls. This maximizes the clean endgame.
decisions.notebook: Core plan: control weather with Politoed and clean with Swift Swim Basculegion; preserve Basculegion when practical. Mega Charizard Y resets sun on Mega entry, so restore rain afterward. Whimsicott supplies priority Tailwind, Taunt, and Encore. Revealed sets: Charizard-Mega-Y—Heat Wave, Solar Beam, Scorching Sands, Protect; Venusaur—Sludge Bomb, Solar Beam, Weather Ball, Protect, Life Orb/Chlorophyll; Goodra-Hisui—Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Flamethrower, Protect, Sitrus Berry/Sap Sipper; Dragapult—Phantom Force, Dragon Darts, U-turn, Will-O-Wisp, Spell Tag/Infiltrator. Respect Garganacl Wide Guard and Tinkaton Fake Out/Feint later. In rain, Politoed Weather Ball strongly threatens Mega Charizard Y. With two allies fainted, boosted Last Respects is preferred for Dragapult.

reflections.summary: Bringing the fragile Sun mode (Charizard-Y and Venusaur) into Politoed and Basculegion allowed Politoed to easily override Sun with manual Rain Dance, enabling Swift Swim Basculegion to sweep with powered-up Last Respects.
reflections.adjustment: Lead Dragapult and Goodra-Hisui to apply direct neutral pressure without relying on Chlorophyll, holding Mega Charizard-Y in the back purely to steal weather after Politoed uses Rain Dance.
reflections.notebook: Opponent roster facts: Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster: Tailwind, Taunt, Encore, Moonblast), Politoed (Sitrus Berry, Drizzle: Rain Dance, Weather Ball, Icy Wind, Protect), Basculegion (Adamant, Life Orb, Swift Swim: Wave Crash, Last Respects, Aqua Jet, Protect), Metagross (Shuca Berry, Clear Body: Meteor Mash, Stomping Tantrum, Rock Slide, Protect). Delphox and Tsareena were benched in G1. Politoed actively uses manual Rain Dance to counteract Drought. Plan: Avoid early Venusaur commits; leverage Dragapult and Goodra-Hisui to handle Politoed/Basculegion under non-rain before bringing Charizard-Y to overwrite weather.

reflections.summary: Won because Politoed repeatedly reclaimed rain from Mega Charizard Y, enabling Basculegion’s boosted Last Respects to remove Goodra-Hisui and Dragapult before rain-boosted Weather Ball finished the sun core. The four brought suited this matchup, and foregoing a Mega evolution did not hinder the plan.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same rain four if the opponent repeats this composition, but preserve Basculegion by using Protect while Politoed resets rain rather than attacking into an expected Venusaur Protect; this retains the Swift Swim cleaner for the final turn.
reflections.notebook: Opponent uses Mega Charizard Y entry to retake weather and Protects with both Charizard and Venusaur to stall or punish direct attacks. Preserve Politoed as the weather-reset piece, and consider Basculegion Protect alongside Rain Dance when sun is active. The non-Mega rain composition is well suited to the revealed Charizard Y/Venusaur/Dragapult/Goodra mode.
